newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices close down on crackdown fears.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices close down on crackdown fears.

text.p: China's stock indices closed sharply down on Tuesday on renewed fears of new measures to cool down trading, brokers said.
In Shanghai, the domestic A share index ended down 35.263 points, or 2.65 percent, at 1,295.905 and the foreign currency B share index lost 0.827 points, or 0.96 percent, to 85.321.
In Shenzhen, the A share index plunged 19.21 points, or 4.31 percent, to 426.45 points and the B share index lost 3.66 points, or 2.43 percent, to 147.11.

Renewed market rumours have it that Beijing will shortly announce a three-day settlement system to replace the present one-day system on the A share markets to slow down the pace of speculative fund movements.
Other rumours said several major brokerages would be banned from trading stocks on their own behalf. Officials have declined to comment.

Last week, Beijing announced a ban on state banks trading on the stock markets. It was the latest of a series of measures which have terminated the bull run of the early months of this year in which share prices rose over 50 percent on average.
"Renewed rumours greatly hurt market sentiment, already weak due to a series of offical crackdown measures," one Shanghai trader said.
"The potential for further falls on the A share markets is still great but that for the B share markets will be limited," he said.
Brokers said they believed the Shanghai B share index would find support at the 85-point level but the A share index could fall more than 10 percent if new measures were announced.
The B share market is technically restricted to foreign investors but mainland Chinese trade on the market through various channels.
"Talk of an imminent government announcement on punishing misbehaving brokerages is keeping buyers off the markets," a Shenzhen-based trader at China Guotai Securities said.
"We are all quite certain the clampdown will take place, it's just a matter of when the government chooses to announce it," an analyst at the China Securities Co said.
Brokers said they expected the Shenzhen A share market to fall more than 15 percent in the next several weeks, but foresaw a flatter B index slide.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber Co was the biggest loser on Shanghai's B share market on Tuesday, plunging $0.056, or 9.75 percent, to $0.518 on volume of 618,300 shares on institutional liquidation.
Shanghai Jiafeng Co was the worst A share performer, falling 0.56 yuan to hit a 10-percent limit-down level of 5.02 yuan.
On Shenzhen's B share market, the biggest loser was SEZ Real Estate and Properties Group Co Ltd which dived HK$0.26, or 7.54 percent, to HK$3.19.
The B share in Beijing Orient Electronics Group Co made its debut in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ending at HK$3.91 compared with an offer price of HK$3.08.
